concepts.def: Behaviour breaking the formal laws of a society and punishable by the state; varies across time and place.
Behaviour breaking informal norms but not always laws; relative to time, place and audience.
Durkheim (1895): crime is inevitable and functional; boundary maintenance, social change, adaptation.
Merton (1938): blocked legitimate routes to success cause innovation (crime); also retreatism, ritualism, rebellion, conformity.
Becker (1963) Outsiders: deviance results from successful application of a label rather than the act itself.
Crime is a product of capitalist inequality; selective enforcement targets working-class crimes over corporate harm.
